subject: Private deployment IaC: module refactor, credential scoping, and CI resilience
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <sre-lead@acmeco.com>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deploy: module refactor + minimal credential surface

Maya —

Thanks for taking this. We’re prepping to onboard Redwood into our VPC/on-prem bundle for a production pilot. Two items that are high priority from our side: credential scoping for least privilege and making the Terraform/Helm modules easier to consume for our platform team (we run a custom bootstrap).

At a high level:
- We need module interfaces that avoid cluster-admin and instead accept a minimal role binding spec from the consumer.
- CI must surface any secret leaks (e.g., provider tokens left in state or helm values).
- For audited runs, we want explicit enablement of flow logs and a plan for retention of audit logs.

Can you share how you envision module contracts and any CI gate checks you’d propose? I attached a short deck with our constraints.

--Alex
Alex Rivera
SRE Lead, Acme Corporation
Attachment: acme-iac-constraints.pdf (pdf)

From: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <sre-lead@acmeco.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: module refactor + minimal credential surface

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. I read the deck and copied Hannah (security) and Karthik (infra) so we can propose a concrete interface. Quick replies to your points:

- Module contract: we prefer a small, opinionated input schema (VPC IDs, subnet tags, and a minimal k8s role-binding blob) rather than trying to create resources that overwrite customer RBAC. That keeps our modules idempotent and audit-friendly.
- Credential scoping: rather than cluster-admin we will accept a namespaced service account ARN/subject plus a minimal set of IAM policies. We'll provide an example policy and a validation tool in CI.
- CI gates: terraform plan output parsing, helm value diffs, secret scanner on staged manifests, and a post-apply verification job that checks flow-logs and route table tagging.

Deliverables I propose by EOD Wednesday:
1) A sample module interface (tf input vars + docs).
2) An example IAM scope (least-privilege example).
3) CI gating checklist and a small prototype script for the secret scanner.

Is there any additional compliance evidence you need for SOC2 Type II before we start a sandbox rollout?

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-17T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: module refactor + minimal credential surface

Following up with some technical specifics and a diff. Key notes:

- Terraform module interface: propose splitting into two modules: network-bootstrap (VPC/subnets/flow log hooks) and runtime-install (helm release + k8s manifests). The runtime module should not create RBAC; it should accept a "consumer_rbac" var that is only applied as a namespaced role binding.
- State handling: we recommend remote state with KMS-encrypted backend and a lifecycle policy to rotate backend access keys. Do not embed provider credentials in modules; instead use a provider alias pattern in the consumer's environment.
- Helm: use values schema validation (helm plugin) in CI to reject unknown top-level fields; that catches accidental secret injection.

I've attached a small patch that refactors the current runtime module to accept a consumer_rbac blob and to remove cluster-wide role creation. Also included: iam-scope-example.yaml with a minimium policy for the SA.

Attachments: priv-module-interface.patch (text), iam-scope-example.yaml (yaml)

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this looks promising. A couple of constraints from our security team:

- Audit evidence: we need plan/apply logs with module-level granularity for the pilot window (90 days). Can your remote-state approach emit an event/metadata we can ship to our SIEM?
- Flow logs: we require per-subnet flow logs retained for 180 days for the pilot.
- Key management: any KMS keys used for state encryption must be customer-controlled (or have a documented key handshake).

If you can confirm those three items and provide the sample IAM scope we can move to scheduling a sandbox deploy next week.

-Alex

Alex / team —

Security here. Quick confirmation against your asks:

- Plan/apply logs: we can emit run metadata and change diffs to a secure S3 bucket with event notifications. We'll include module path and diff summary so your SIEM can parse module-level granularity. We'll also generate a signed attest artifact for each apply.
- Flow logs retention: we'll add retention policy toggles in the network-bootstrap module; default will set 180 days for the pilot.
- KMS ownership: customer-controlled KMS is supported; we will include a documented key handshake and an integration test in CI that validates access before any apply.

CI gating checklist (high-level):
- terraform fmt & validate
- terraform plan (fail on provider creds in output)
- secret-scan (trufflehog-based) on plan+helm rendered manifests
- post-apply verifier (ensures flow logs active, route tables tagged)
- evidence bundle upload to secure bucket + signed attest artifact

I linked SUP-3421 for the CI gating tickets and a doc draft for the evidence bundle. I'll spin up the CI gate tickets once we agree.

Attachments: ci-gate-checklist.md (markdown)

Kimberly Park
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
